create.name: Matthew Sockolov
create.bio:
Matthew Sockolov is an American Buddhist meditation teacher who, with his wife Elizabeth, runs One Mind Dharma, a project that began in 2011 as a small mindfulness blog and grew into a full online home for guided practice, talks and courses. He first met Buddhist ideas as a teenager through a Thich Nhat Hanh book, later trained at Against the Stream in Los Angeles and at Spirit Rock, which empowered him to teach, and has studied with Thanissaro Bhikkhu at Metta Forest Monastery. Since 2013 he has guided sitting groups, first in Los Angeles and later in Northern California.

Now living in Playa del Carmen in Mexico, he teaches almost entirely online. His weekly groups include a Thursday morning sit, a longer Tuesday evening session with a dharma talk, and a Friday group shaped by the everyday-awareness approach of Sayadaw U Tejaniya, all offered on a donation basis. He writes and records the One Mind Dharma podcast, whose recent series looks at how well-known teachers meditate, and offers one-to-one mindfulness coaching. His six-week online course grew out of his book Practicing Mindfulness, and he is also the author of A Mindfulness for Beginners Journal.

books.title: A Mindfulness for Beginners Journal: Prompts and Practices for Living in the Moment
books.author: Matthew Sockolov
books.description: A guided journal for people new to mindful living, pairing short exercises with space to write. Prompts move from focusing on the breath to noticing thoughts and treating oneself kindly.

courses.title: Practicing Mindfulness Online Course
courses.description: A self-paced six-week course built on his book, with three days of practice a week. Each day brings a guided meditation, a short video on carrying the practice into daily life, and questions for reflection, with the teacher available by message.

courses.title: Tuesday Sit
courses.description: A weekly online evening group: half an hour of sitting, a short pause, then a dharma talk and open discussion. Offered on a donation basis, with links sent out each week.

courses.title: Thursday Morning Meditation
courses.description: A short weekly online sit on Thursday mornings, Pacific time, with a fifteen-minute guided practice, a brief talk and time for questions. Donation-based.

courses.title: Mindfulness Coaching
courses.description: One-to-one online sessions for students who want to deepen a personal practice. Sessions usually combine a brief sit with conversation, and begin with a free introductory call.

free_resources.title: Matthew Sockolov on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: His guided meditations and talks on the free Insight Timer app.

free_resources.title: A Month of Mindfulness
free_resources.description: A free thirty-day email programme for beginners, sending one very short meditation each day. It introduces a different technique daily so newcomers can settle into a routine and find what suits them.

free_resources.title: 30 Day Meditation Challenge
free_resources.description: A long-running free challenge with a daily practice of fifteen to thirty minutes delivered by email. Over the month it covers mindfulness, concentration, compassion and sympathetic joy.

free_resources.title: Intro to Mindfulness
free_resources.description: A free one-week online course with a brief guided meditation and short talks each day. It explains what mindfulness is and how to keep practising afterwards.

free_resources.title: Awareness in Everyday Life
free_resources.description: A free set of more than thirty recorded lessons on the practice style of the Burmese teacher Sayadaw U Tejaniya. The focus is on keeping awareness going through ordinary activity rather than only on the cushion.
